Sound level and spectrum

Calibrated sound meters (A- and C-weighted) with a 1/3-octave spectrum, each read from one lane of the audio bus at its full 48 kHz by Relay's audio core. Add one per place you want to measure, and pick it on a board's sound widgets. Patch a measurement mic to the lane for room SPL; a desk feed measures the mix only.

Stream mix report

While the stream mix carries sound, Relay saves a row a second (loudness, peak, left/right correlation, octave bands) for each captions session, then judges it against your targets. Patch the mix's left and right to two lanes from the same device.

Download CSV

Audio bus

Up to 32 lanes from any input, routed to outputs through one crosspoint matrix.

First setup

Pick the sound device the captions listen to and the one Relay plays alert tones through. You can change both below at any time.

Bus

Each lane is one mono channel of an input, at 48 kHz; the captions, the sound meter, a recorder or an output can each take a lane. The main capture on Audio input is not touched.

Off

Lanes

Patch one channel of an input to a lane, or mix to sum every channel of it. A device is opened once however many lanes use it.

Outputs

An output is a device with up to 32 channels. Its channels are what the crosspoints below feed.

Crosspoints

Output channels down, lanes across: click a square to feed a lane into a channel, and set its gain in dB. A channel mixes every lane fed into it. Save lanes and outputs first; new ones show here once saved.

Target languages

Choose which languages are translated and offered to viewers.

Enabled languages

Every language is translated from the one transcription, a line at a time, so another language costs almost nothing. Turning one off takes effect from the next line. The models are picked on AI models.

Panels

Caption panels on the venue network. Click a panel name to see and change its settings.

Set up a new panel over USB Flash a new or recovered panel from Chrome or Edge with the release’s relay-display.bin. Flash a panel →

Paired panels

No panels have checked in yet.

Panel firmware

One image per kind of panel. Upload that panel's relay-display-app.bin from a release; Relay checks it is a panel image for that board, but the panel decides whether the signature is right and refuses anything not signed with its release key. An update installs at a quiet moment (no new caption line for a while) unless you choose “Update now”.

How panels work

Caption panels on the venue network appear here by themselves. A feed you set is sent to the panel at once; a change made at the panel’s own screen afterwards wins until you set one again. Forgetting a panel that is still switched on brings it straight back, unnamed.

Alerts

The band opens the sender page on a phone and taps a row. Each row is something they can send; each column is a panel or browser screen. Tick a square to send that row to that screen.

Unsaved changes
Alert buttons flash until someone at the screen taps it, then the sender sees where it was seen. Stage messages show words over whatever the screen shows, with nothing to tap, and end on their own. A panel joins when it checks in; a browser screen joins when it is opened at its column’s link. Test shows “Test from Relay” on that one screen for a few seconds.
Settings
If nobody taps. The sender then sees “Not seen” and can send again. The flash is once a second, well under the rate where flashing becomes a seizure risk.
A banner is a strip across the top that stays up longer than a message.
Tapped on the flashing screen instead of a plain acknowledge, so nobody needs a keyboard. The sender sees it next to “Seen”. Up to 6, of 24 characters. Leave it empty for a plain acknowledge.
Otherwise anyone with the sender link can send, so hand it to the band, not the room. With sign-in on, the sender page moves to this panel’s https:// address, and anyone whose role can send alerts may use it, including a Member. Panels send as they always have.

Copy the link from the Build tab first. Use the canvas size your switcher runs at; the overlay is transparent everywhere except the captions.

OBS Studio

Browser source · your canvas size · transparent

  1. Sources → + → Browser. Name it “Relay captions”.
  2. Paste the link into URL. Set width and height to your canvas (Settings → Video → Base resolution).
  3. Untick Shutdown source when not visible so captions do not restart when you change scenes.
  4. Drag it above your camera sources in every scene that needs captions, or put it in a nested scene shared by all of them.

vMix

Web Browser input · 1920 × 1080 · transparent

  1. Add Input → Web Browser, paste the link, and set the size to your output resolution.
  2. Put it on an Overlay channel (1–4) and press it on.
  3. To caption the stream only, take it on the stream output’s overlay channel and leave the projector output clean.

ProPresenter

Web Page object on a Prop · stream Look only

  1. Create a Prop with a Web Page object filling the slide; paste the link.
  2. In Looks, turn Props on for the stream screen and off for the room screens.
  3. Trigger the Prop at the start of the service; it stays up while slides change.

Blackmagic ATEM

Upstream key · switcher format

  1. Chroma green: open the link full-screen on a computer whose HDMI feeds one ATEM input, then use a Chroma key on that input.
  2. Key matte: save two overlays, one with Key matte and one with Black; feed each to its own input and set a Luma key with the black one as fill and the matte as key.
  3. Turn the key on for program. Keep the computer’s screen saver and notifications off.

Recordings & export

Save each run's transcript to disk and export it.

Recording

A recording covers exactly one run — from Start to Stop. Every committed caption line is written to disk as it happens, so a crash mid-event still leaves you the transcript up to that point. Blocked words are removed before anything is written. Off by default: nothing is recorded until you turn this on.
Stored in recordings/

Runs

RunDurationLinesDownload
Nothing recorded yet.

What’s in the export

The zip holds a timestamped transcript-<LANGUAGE>.txt per language, plus, per target language, a pairs-<TARGET>.jsonl (each source line matched to its translation, with a confidence field) and a finetune-<TARGET>.jsonl in OpenAI chat format, ready to upload to a fine-tuning job.
The two feeds carry no shared segment id and are broken into lines independently, so pairs are matched on overlapping time span and every row says how sure the match is. Only the exact ones are carried into the fine-tuning file — the rest stay in the pairs file to be reviewed.

Schedules

Named schedules that start and stop capture and drive signage, boards and call times.

Schedules

Starts and stops capture

Used by

    Delete is refused while anything is listed here; pick another schedule in those places first.

    How schedules work

    Capture starts and stops on its own inside each window of the schedules ticked for it. If it is already running when a window opens, it keeps running and stops at the window’s end. Pressing Stop during a window holds it until the next scheduled start. Starting by hand outside a window is never stopped by a schedule. Windows that overlap or touch run as one session.
    Times follow Relay's time zone, including daylight saving. The machine and the relay must be running for a schedule to fire; a window already under way when the relay starts is picked up, and one missed entirely is skipped.

    Blocked words

    Removed from the transcript and every translation.

    Blocklist

    Edited in blocklist.txt with one word or phrase per line. Changes to the file are picked up within about two seconds, no restart. You can also edit it here.

    How matching works

    Matches are removed outright: no asterisks, no gap, nothing on screen to notice. Case and accents are ignored (nino matches niño) and only whole words match, so ass will not touch class.
    Each feed is filtered on its own, so to remove a word everywhere, list it in each language.

    Credentials

    Keys used by this relay.

    Keys

    Stored server-side in config.json (0600), encrypted with a key kept in this computer's keychain (). Never sent to viewer pages.

    Backup passphrase

    Relay backs up its database every day, encrypted with this computer's key. With a passphrase, a copy can also be restored on another computer. Relay keeps only a key made from it, never the passphrase, so write it down somewhere safe.

    Applies from the next backup. Restore with relay --restore-backup <file> --passphrase with Relay stopped.

    AI models

    Every AI task goes through the one Vercel AI Gateway key. A task can be switched to the OpenAI key instead, and uses it on its own when the Vercel key is not saved. Switching translation does not stop captions.

    Live transcription

    Captions use ElevenLabs Scribe v2 Realtime until Vercel lists Scribe v3 Live; the model moves to v3 Live then. Talkback speaker labels need v3 Live, so talkback has none until then. Talkback uses this transcription unless its own page picks another.

    Text and speech

    Appearance & tuning

    Viewer text size and how caption lines are broken.

    Viewer display

    One time zone for Relay: schedules, signage, boards, call times and YouTube all read it.

    Caption line breaks

    A caption line is committed once its text has been quiet for line break after silence and it ends on a sentence boundary. A line that never reaches one is committed by the force a line break backstop, always at a word boundary so a word is never cut in half. Lower the first for snappier lines; raise the second if you see a sentence split across two lines. In-progress text is already on screen as it streams, so a generous backstop costs nothing. Changing these restarts live sessions.

    Planning Center

    Show the service plan on panels and screens, and run Services LIVE from here.

    Service you are viewing

    Plan and time come from Planning Center. The Service, Team and inputs, and Rundown tabs show this choice: the order of service with Next and Previous, who is on each channel, and the /screen rundown.

    Plan: Relay uses the plan dated today. Pick another to use it until the day ends. Service time: Automatic picks the running service, else the next one.

    Next and Previous work only while the person who made the token has control, the same as a panel's press. Every press is listed under Panels.

    Service types Relay follows

    Relay reads plans only from the types you tick, and panels can only pick these. Untick the ones you never run. The list comes from your Planning Center account.

    Panels

    Panels show the plan and can press Next and Previous as the person who made the token.

    Presses from panels

    Input channels on the board

    Add the input channels you want to track, then assign each one to the positions that use it. An input channel can serve positions from several service types, so one shared by Sunday and Youth is set up once.

    Add an input channel from the console

    Choose from the channels Relay knows. Their names come from the gear and are the same on every page. One that is not listed can be typed in below.

    Older mic settings are still in use:

    They list mics by position instead of channels. Move them to the board to see and change them here.

    Relay gives every confirmed person in a position one of its input channels, drawn at random once and then kept, so nobody changes mid-service. It only changes when someone confirms or drops out, or when you press Shuffle. People past the last input channel get none.

    The rundown on /screen

    /screen is a display-only page for the production team's monitor: the order of service with clock times, who is on which mic, the song leader and the sermon notes. It never scrolls and has no buttons, so everything is fitted to one screen.

    Off by default. It shows volunteers' names, photos, mics and sermon notes, so it is available on this network only. Relay refuses it through remote access, and the panels and audience caption pages never carry any of it.

    What the screen shows

    Every item is fitted to the screen. The short list stays large and readable from far away.
    Per position groups everyone on a team under their role.
    Show one team only, such as Worship for the stage monitor.
    Automatic picks whichever service LIVE is running, else the next one.
    Open it in a browser on the screen's computer. Team and service time are part of the link, so each screen can have its own.

    Where Relay finds names and notes

    The rundown reads these from your Planning Center plan. Change them if your church labels things differently.

    Relay reads the first line of this note on a song item.
    Used when a song has no leader note.
    Taken from the current item, or the next one that has it.

    Plan files on signage screens

    Copies the pictures and videos attached to the current or next plan, and to its items, into the signage media library, and can keep a signage playlist called Planning Center plan in step with them. Relay looks again every five minutes and when you press Sync now. A file is downloaded once and again only when it changes in Planning Center. Off until you switch it on. Needs the Signage module.

    From api.planningcenteronline.com/personal_access_tokens.

    Slide view and lobby

    Three separate ways to get ProPresenter’s slides in front of people who are not at the ProPresenter computer. Each has its own settings and works without the others.

    1

    Slide view

    A live picture of the slide that is up and the one coming next, with the countdown on it, for anyone who cannot see the screen: the sound desk, the green room, a tablet backstage.

    ProPresenter→Relay→A web page at /stage
    2

    Lobby rotation

    Relay moves a ProPresenter announcement playlist along by itself, one slide every few seconds, so lobby screens that ProPresenter drives never sit on one slide. Use this when your lobby TVs are fed by ProPresenter. It does not start on its own: press Start.

    Relaypresses Next onan announcement playlist→ProPresenter lobby screens
    ProPresenter does not say which playlists are for the lobby, so you pick.
    If something else is put on the announcements layer, the rotation waits and carries on when it is cleared.
    Not running.
    3

    Signage copy

    Copies each slide of a playlist into Relay’s signage as a picture, so TVs on Relay signage can show the announcements without ProPresenter. Use this when your lobby TVs are signage screens, not ProPresenter outputs. Needs the Signage module.

    ProPresenter playlistcopied every two minutesRelay signage→Signage TVs

    ProPresenter

    Follow the slide that is up, show lyrics on screens and panels, and put a message on the stage display.

    Now

    Connection

    Relay can know several ProPresenter computers. The primary one drives the show: lyrics, timers, slide tags, the lobby and the Planning Center link all follow it. Make another computer the primary to control it.
    In ProPresenter, open Settings → Network, switch Enable Network on, and copy the port it shows: the port is set per install, so Relay assumes none. ProPresenter’s API has no password, so Relay only ever talks out to the address typed here, and anyone who can reach that port can control ProPresenter: keep it on the production network. The ProPresenter machine’s firewall must let this computer reach that port.

    Safety

    Lyrics feed

    Song lyrics are licensed. The feed is off for the public phone viewer unless you switch it on, and anyone on the network who opens the link can read it when it is on.
    A presentation is a song when its file is in this library, or when its parts are named Verse, Chorus, Bridge and the like.

    Timers on panels

    A caption panel set to Timers shows ProPresenter timers large: white while one runs, amber and then red as a countdown nears zero, and red with a minus sign once it is over. The panel counts the seconds itself between Relay's updates. A panel can use its own settings instead: open it under Panels.
    Time left, as minutes:seconds (2:00) or seconds (90). Red cannot be earlier than amber.
    Tick up to four. With none ticked, panels show the first four timers ProPresenter has.

    Stage message

    An alert can also appear here: tick Also show on the ProPresenter stage display on its button under Alerts. It is cleared when the alert is acknowledged.

    Slide-note tags

    A tag in a slide's notes in ProPresenter does something in Relay when that slide goes live. Relay only reads the notes, it never changes them. [relay:lyrics] on a slide, or [relay-deck:lyrics] in any slide of a presentation for every slide of it that has no tag of its own. The tags are capture-start, capture-stop (Relay's own captioning, not ProPresenter's capture), lyrics, captions, lang=es and alert=Button name. With the Signage module on, signage-screen=Screen:Playlist, signage-group=Group:Playlist and signage-all=Playlist switch what screens play; signage-push, signage-captions, signage-service and signage-resume (each also as -screen and -group) take a screen over and give it back. The guide has the full list.
    A slide's tags run only after it has stayed live this long, so a fast run through the slides runs one set, not all of them. Moving to a slide with the same tags runs nothing again.

    Planning Center link

    Matches the plan's items to ProPresenter's presentations, shows both sides while a service runs, and can let ProPresenter move Planning Center's LIVE item. Both switches are off until you turn them on. Needs ProPresenter and Planning Center connected.
